# Susan Baker

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c18 P58](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0058)</sub>
- **Status:** Unmarried spinster  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c38 P39](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0039)</sub>
- **Origin:** The Glen  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052)</sub>
- **Role:** Maid-of-all-work and domestic helper  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c19 P0](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Susan Baker is a grim-faced, elderly spinster.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052)_

## Personality

Susan is a kind-hearted, brisk, and fiercely loyal woman who devotedly serves Anne Blythe. She takes immense pride in her household duties and feels deep affection for Anne and her baby. While capable of intense emotion and weeping during times of tragedy, she remains practical and quick to take charge of kitchen and domestic matters. She occasionally reflects on marriage with a mixture of humor, frankness, and resignation.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c19 P0](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0000), [v4 c19 P5](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0005), [v4 c19 P10](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0010), [v4 c19 P17](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0017), [v4 c38 P39](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0039), [v4 c38 P41](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0041)_

## History

Susan Baker, an elderly spinster living in the Glen, was installed as a maid-of-all-work at the little house of dreams for Dr. Gilbert Blythe and his wife Anne. Within a few weeks of her arrival, she came to adore young Mrs. Doctor with blind fervor. When Marilla Cuthbert arrived prior to the birth of Anne's first child, Susan initially regarded her with slight jealousy before reconciling with her after realizing Marilla would not interfere in kitchen affairs. During the tense night of Anne's labor, Susan sat in the kitchen with cotton wool in her ears and an apron over her head while praying fiercely for Anne's safety. Following the child's birth, Susan immediately took charge of domestic affairs so Anne could focus on her baby. When the infant tragically died, Susan wept alongside Marilla out of heartbreak for Anne. She continued her steadfast service to the Blythe family, engaging in conversations about local marriages and community affairs with Anne and Miss Cornelia Bryant.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c19 P0](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0000), [v4 c19 P1](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0001), [v4 c19 P5](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0005), [v4 c19 P9](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0009), [v4 c19 P10](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0010), [v4 c19 P17](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0017), [v4 c38 P38](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0038), [v4 c38 P39](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0039)_

## Background by volume

- Hails from the Glen  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052)</sub>
- Had a sister who was a great talker and married James Clow
- Was once proposed to and engaged to Malcolm Andres

## Quotes

> Very poorly—very poorly, Cornelia. I am afraid she will soon be in heaven, poor thing!  <sub>[v4 c18 P55](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0055)</sub>

> Do not tell me, that God could be so cruel as to take that darling lamb from us when we all love her so much.  <sub>[v4 c19 P5](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0005)</sub>

> Now for breakfast, I am of the opinion that we will all be glad of a bite and sup. You tell young Mrs. Doctor not to worry about a single thing—Susan is at the helm. You tell her just to think of her baby.  <sub>[v4 c19 P10](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0010)</sub>

> Well, Mrs. Doctor, dear, it does NOT seem to me fair. Here is me, who never said a word against the men, and I cannot get married nohow. And there is Cornelia Bryant, who is never done abusing them, and all she has to do is to reach out her hand and pick one up, as it were. It is a very strange world, Mrs. Doctor, dear.  <sub>[v4 c38 P39](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0039)</sub>

> Yes, but, Mrs. Doctor, dear, there is neither marrying nor giving in marriage there.  <sub>[v4 c38 P41](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0041)</sub>
